description: A user changes a field of a company record. Explain how a corresponding entry appears on that record's timeline: which in-process listener reacts to the change, what decides whether a timeline entry is produced at all, how the work is moved off the request path, which worker class does the write, and where the timeline row is finally persisted. Also explain why writing that timeline row does not cause the timeline machinery to trigger itself again.
anchor_note: non-bug task: root_cause_symbols holds the anchor (entry point / changed symbol); RC metrics are reported for category A only
alternatives: Records of objects with audit logging also enqueue an event-log job from the same handleEvent (isAuditLogBatchEvent), a parallel branch.
Junction-rule payloads (e.g. note/task targets) produce entries on the related record's timeline via buildPayloadsForJunctionRule.

source.verification: Run timeline-activity-write-path.integration-spec.ts; or confirm via cited lines that the queue-add string equals the @Process argument.
